pillar_reactions.evidence: No pillar was delivered on this call. The rep deferred the whole presentation to the joint call with the wife: 'Trevor will take you through everything, that's what I'll run you through on Friday, like how it works, and if that all works for you, then we'll get you started on Friday.'
Nutrition was covered only as discovery ('is it only whole foods for you?'), never presented as a component of the programme.

The rep summarised accountability back as the prospect's own diagnosed gap - 'it comes down to having accountability, having a routine in place, actually have someone sort of giving you the guidance that you need' - and the prospect agreed emphatically, but it was never delivered as a pillar of the offer.

anchors.raw: he inspired me to go out and buy, you know, various kettlebells and whatnot, which honestly I've had them about a month and all they are is collecting dust. haven't even touched them.
anchors.note: He already owns the kettlebells, a home gym, a state-of-the-art elliptical and twelve years of an unused gym membership. Every one of those was a cheaper attempt at the same outcome and every one failed, which is simultaneously the best argument for buying accountability and the loudest evidence in his own head that spending money on this does not work for him. Nobody named that tension on the call.

anchors.raw: As I transition and retire, of course, the budget is going to be a lot tighter.
anchors.note: He is nine weeks from ending a full-time salary and moving to part-time work plus pensions. Whatever number is presented on Friday lands against a shrinking budget he has already flagged, and against a wife who currently believes the call was a scam.

anchors.raw: It would be in the four figures, somewhere between 1,000 and 6,000 or so.
anchors.note: The most damaging anchor on the call was set by the rep himself. The prospect now has $1,000-$1,500 as the bottom of the range and repeated it back as '1500 to 5k a year'. The real floor is $6,000 for six months, so Friday's presentation has to climb over an anchor Primal created.

anchors.raw: I've, you know, gone out, purchased some, you know, protein supplement, you know, dimetized powder, and I just bought some creatine and whatnot. So, you know, I'm willing to commit and get serious about this.
anchors.note: He habitually pays for health products - 'I bought various supplements, probably take entirely too many' - and bought the kettlebells purely on Trevor's inspiration. Willingness to spend on this category is established; the scale is not.

unmet_demand.want: His wife coached alongside him. He raised it four separate times - 'I want her as well', 'I want her to do the same', 'I want my wife to be on the journey with me' - and it is the condition on which the whole decision rests.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme as sold is one-to-one with Trevor for one person. The rep noticed the question ('I don't know. Does she have to have a separate program?') and never answered it, on this call or by promising an answer on Friday. If the answer is a second $6,000 that is a $12,000 ask against a retiring budget.

unmet_demand.want: Help with twelve years of shift-driven chronic sleep deprivation, which he described as the thing 'tearing me apart' and which prescribed medication has not fixed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Sleep is not one of the three pillars the reps present, and the rep did not respond to the disclosure at all beyond acknowledging that the shift pattern was ending. It is plausible the coaching does address sleep, but nothing was said.

unmet_demand.want: Meaningful reduction in his multigenerational cancer risk, which is the deepest motivator he expressed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: A kettlebell and nutrition programme cannot promise this, and correctly nobody offered to. But it means the outcome he most wants is one the offer can only address obliquely, and the gap was never acknowledged or reframed.
